subject: DPA: request for verified deletion manifest, snapshots & legal-hold workflow
messages:
From: Marta Silva <marta.silva@helixdata.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@helixdata.com
Date: Fri, 8 Sep 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: proof of deletion + retention carveouts

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this — our security & privacy team reviewed the DPA and have a few non-standard asks we need to reconcile before we can sign:

1) Verified deletion manifest: we need per-tenant receipts for deletion requests that show deletion_id, timestamp (UTC), resource identifiers (snapshot id or tenant id), and a cryptographic digest proving the object referenced was removed (SHA-256 or equivalent). We may request these receipts up to 30 days post-deletion.

2) Snapshots/backups: for EU-hosted tenants we want a 90-day snapshot retention for auditability, but we also need a mechanism to accelerate purges on request (for regulatory takedown). Please confirm whether backups are under the same onshore residency guarantees and whether you can produce evidence when they are purged.

3) Legal hold: we need a formal process to put a tenant on legal hold that pauses automated deletion and documents the hold window. The hold should be triggered by a written notice to security@redwood.com with a ticket number and reference key.

Attached: audit_requirements_v1.pdf with example manifest fields.

Can you confirm what you can provide as standard vs what would be a custom addendum?

Best,
Marta Silva
Head of Privacy, HelixData

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marta Silva <marta.silva@helixdata.com>
Cc: legal@helixdata.com
Date: Fri, 8 Sep 2028 11:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: proof of deletion + retention carveouts

Marta — thanks, very clear. Quick summary of what Redwood can commit to today and a couple of constraints so we can get to language:

- Tiered erasure profile (what we propose as standard):
  * Production tenant data: deletion initiated within 30 days of request; live data removed from serving layer immediately once request authorized.
  * Non-production (sandboxes): retention default 7 days unless customer elects longer.
  * Snapshots/backups: retention policy configurable per-tenant; default snapshot TTL is 180 days.

- Verified deletion manifest: we can generate a per-deletion receipt containing deletion_id, UTC timestamp, affected resource ids, and a manifest-hash. For privacy reasons we do not publish raw object contents; the manifest-hash is a SHA-256 over a canonical manifest (deletion_id + resource ids + timestamp). Receipts are available for 30 days post-deletion via secure link.

- Accelerated purge: we can initiate expedited purge for onshore backups when given a documented request; purge completion will emit a manifest entry and confirmation token. Due to provider snapshot semantics some cloud snapshots may require an additional coordinated job to fully remove underlying blocks — we guarantee the manifest token once our purge job completes.

- Legal hold: we accept written hold notices at security@redwood.com. Holds must include tenant id, reason, and a reference number; Redwood will suspend automated retention-driven purges and record the hold in the audit log. Holds will be lifted only when we receive express release or a court order is closed.

I've attached a short draft redline of the manifest format and proposed DPA language (redwood-deletion-manifest-draft.docx).

If ok I will loop in Engineering and Ops (Neha) to confirm the snapshot purge timing and manifest distribution SLA.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: legal@helixdata.com
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Silva <marta.silva@helixdata.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Sep 2028 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: proof of deletion + retention carveouts

Soojin / Marta — thanks. A couple clarifying asks from our side:

- The manifest-hash approach sounds acceptable in principle. Can Redwood confirm whether the manifest-hash can be verified against a previously provided snapshot manifest? We need chain-of-custody assurance.

- For EU-only tenants, we require that any backup or snapshot retention is processed on EU infrastructure and that deletion of backups is performed within the same residency boundary. Please confirm where the purge job runs.

- We also need a 30-day window to request full deletion receipts and an option to require a certified destruction letter for high-risk data subjects.

Attached: gdpr_req.docx (redlines).

Regards,
HelixData Legal

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: legal@helixdata.com, Marta Silva <marta.silva@helixdata.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Sep 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: proof of deletion + retention carveouts

Looping in Neha (ops) and Jordan (legal ops) to lock down the operational wording. High-level counter-proposals below; I placed proposed language in an attached text file (proposed-dpa-schedule-redline.txt).

Counter-proposals (summary):
- Chain-of-custody: Redwood will persist a signed manifest (manifest.json) at time of deletion that contains deletion_id, tenant_id, timestamp_utc, resource_ids, and a manifest-hash (SHA-256). Customers may request the manifest within 30 days. The manifest can be used to verify that the resource ids referenced are the subjects of the purge; the manifest-hash cannot be reversed to recover content.

- Residency: For EU-designated tenants, backup snapshots will be stored in EU zones only. Expedited purges for EU backups will be executed on EU infrastructure and we will provide a completion manifest.

- Certified destruction: Redwood will provide a certified deletion confirmation letter for requests flagged as High-Risk within 10 business days after purge completion. Standard manifests are available within 72 hours of purge job completion.

As a next step Neha — can you confirm the 72-hour SLA and any known exceptions (provider retention, immutable snapshots, cross-zone replication)? Jordan — can you confirm if the proposed hold/release wording meets legal's ask.

Thanks,
Soojin

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Silva <marta.silva@helixdata.com>, legal@helixdata.com, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Sep 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: proof of deletion + retention carveouts — ops clarifications

Thanks — a few operational notes to make sure the language is implementable:

- Provider snapshot semantics: Many cloud snapshot systems create delta fragments and garbage-collect asynchronously. For some block-level snapshot backends a full physical reclaim can take up to 7 days after our purge job completes (we invoke provider APIs immediately); however, our internal logical index will reflect deletion immediately and we will not serve content after the deletion timestamp.

- 72-hour manifest SLA: Ops can generate and sign the manifest within 72 hours of the purge job completing in our systems. For EU onshore purges the purge job will run in EU regions; the 72-hour window starts when the onshore purge job is kicked and completes when our manifest is generated and uploaded to the secure tenant portal/Drive.

- Manifest format: we will use a canonical JSON manifest where manifest-hash = SHA256(canonical_manifest_string). We can provide partial examples in the ops playbook (attached ops-playbook.md). Note: we intentionally do not include content blobs in manifests — only identifiers + metadata.

- Legal hold: holds will be recorded as a ticket (JIRA SEC-xxxx) and will pause future retention-driven purges. Holds do not retroactively restore deleted content; if a hold is placed after deletion, HelixData may request a certified destruction letter instead.

Operational exceptions: immutable archival tiers (if customer explicitly stores snapshots in archival tier) may require up to 14 calendar days to complete a physical wipe. We'll call these out as carveouts.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marta Silva <marta.silva@helixdata.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@helixdata.com
Date: Sun, 10 Sep 2028 14:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: proof of deletion + retention carveouts — acceptance pending minor edits

Soojin / team — this looks reasonable and addresses our core concerns. A couple final edits from Legal:

- Add explicit language that Redwood will provide the manifest-hash and the signed canonical manifest within 72 hours of purge completion for EU tenants.
- Document the 14-day archival-exception window in an appendix and require Redwood to notify HelixData within 24 hours if an archival-tier exception applies to a purge.
- Legal hold: HelixData will provide a reference key and Jira ticket; Redwood must confirm receipt within 48 hours and mark the tenant as on-hold in the audit log.

If you incorporate those small edits into the DPA redline we can proceed to final legal review. Appreciate your responsiveness — please also schedule a 30 minute sync next week to walk through the ops playbook.

Best,
Marta Silva
Head of Privacy, HelixData

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marta Silva <marta.silva@helixdata.com>, legal@helixdata.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Sep 2028 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: proof of deletion + retention carveouts — confirm next steps

Thanks Marta — we will accept those edits and update the redline. Next steps:

1) Redwood will produce an updated DPA redline (incorporating 72-hour EU manifest commitment, appendix for 14-day archival exceptions, and 48-hour hold-ack workflow) by Tue 2028-09-12 EOD PT.
2) Ops (Neha) will prepare a 30-minute playbook walkthrough (Jira: SEC-1198) for Wed 2028-09-13 — invite sent.
3) Upon acceptance of the redline HelixData legal will request the certified destruction letter template where applicable (we will supply a draft).

I'll attach the edited redline to the DPA and send a follow-up. Thanks all.

Soojin
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
